1.why: All six screens show a static, uncluttered layout with no animations, moving images, or pop-ups.

2.why: Bold headings, high-contrast teal primary buttons, and highlighted safety/rule boxes make key elements stand out.

3.why: Each step has a single clear title, one main field, and one primary button, so the needed action is immediately visible.

4.why: The user must remember and apply multiple password composition rules (14+ chars, upper, lower, number, symbol, no spaces) across a multi-step flow.

5.why: No password-manager, autofill, or “remember me” controls appear on any screen.

6.why: The UI presents no saved accounts, familiar labels, or recognizable prior items for the user to identify.

7.why: Instructional text is brief and plainly worded on every step, though the raw hex tokens are long.

8.why: No error states or error messages are shown in any of the provided screenshots.

9.why: Placeholders and the password-rules box give partial guidance, but no concrete input examples are supplied.

10.why: The flow offers no choice among password, code, face, or other login methods—only a single recovery-code path.

11.why: Each screen presents essentially one primary action and at most one secondary link, avoiding choice overload.

12.why: The final screen explicitly confirms the password was saved and the user may sign in; intermediate titles also reflect progress.

13.why: Safety-reminder callouts and the password-rules box supply short tips on each relevant step.

14.why: A “Start over” link is present on the recovery-code screens, letting the user restart after a mistake.

15.why: All screens share identical header, card layout, button style, and safety-reminder placement, keeping the design consistent.
